house: John Moulton Homestead, House (HABS WY-152-A), Mormon Row, Kelly vicinity, Teton County, WY

source.credit: Historic American Buildings Survey, National Park Service; Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division

origin: the south-west corner of the house's outer box: x = 0 at the mud room's west outer face, y = 0 at the main block's south outer face
compass: the sheets are drawn with west at the top: plan up is west, plan right is north, plan down is east (from sheet 2's elevations: the front door and porch steps are on the east elevation, the mud room's three windows on the west)

outside.note: outer faces: 30'-1" (y) by 32'-9" (x) with the mud room, from the written dimension strings; the mud room is the part x < 7.83, y 7.0 to 23.0

doors.note: front door, east; steps down outside
north side, onto a stoop with steps; drawn swinging both ways (a door and a screen door)
a narrow double-acting door drawn through the thick old west wall; read as a door between the two, not certain
the foot of the stair up
the head of the stair down to the basement
a small door drawn at the closet's corner by the hall wall
a low door into the inaccessible eave space north of the hall, which is not a room of this key

openings.note: no wall or door is drawn between the kitchen and the lobby east of the stair

windows.note: an inside window, from the small room into the mud room

stairs.note: one straight flight rising east from a landing by the mud room door; it arrives in the second floor hall
under the flight up, rising west to east; its head is the door from the lobby

notes: Dimensions written on the sheets: the outer strings (30'-1" on the west, east and second floor; 32'-9" on the south) and each room's size. Everything else was measured off the 1-bit TIFF at 100 pixels a foot (the scale, checked against the dimension strings to within 1%).

Room outlines are the clear floor between the inner edges of the drawn wall lines, found by flood fill on the sheet; they agree with the written room sizes within 0.25 ft (the mud room measures 7.2 by 14.6 against 7'-5" by 14'-8").

Door and window positions are the middle of the opening on the wall's centre line; widths are the clear opening between jambs, from the dimension strings where the strings give them (front door, east and south windows, the mud room's windows) and measured elsewhere (about +-0.2 ft).

Heights are not written: measured off section A-A (sheet 3) at the same scale. Main floor to ceiling 7.75; main floor to second floor 8.77; second floor to its flat ceiling 7.15 (the bedrooms' outer parts are under the roof slope, closed off as inaccessible eaves); basement floor 7.43 below the main floor, its ceiling 6.6 over it.
The second floor plan carries no x string; it was placed by the hall's east wall and the stair in section A-A (x 29.95 and 16.85), to about +-0.25 ft.
The research note (research/blueprint-sources.md) says the mud room is on the north; the elevations put it on the west. This key follows the elevations.
Only the basement room is walkable below; the rest of the basement plan is marked inaccessible (crawl space). The west attic over the mud room and the eaves are inaccessible and not rooms here.
Two doors are marked uncertain: a 1.5 ft double-acting door between the mud room and kitchen, and a small closet door upstairs. A judge may leave them out of P4.
